verdicts.reason: This change brings back a known bug: panel config gets written into the query's shared data. `applyFieldOverrides` now merges the panel's field config straight into the field objects inside nested frames, and those objects come from the source query. Before, it copied each field and its config first. Without the copy, one panel's settings leak into data that other panels and the query runner also read. The change also deletes the regression test that checked the input frames stay untouched, so nothing will catch the leak.

findings.message: Nested frames are now changed in place. `defaultsDeep` writes this panel's resolved field config straight into `valueField.config`, and `newValues[idx]` holds the original `nestedFrame` object. The removed comment and test explain why that's a problem: nested frames, such as the sparkline frames built by the "Time series to table" transformation, use the source query's own field objects. So this panel's config (unit, displayName, overrides) leaks into data that other panels and the query runner still read. Because `defaultsDeep` only fills undefined keys, the first panel to run also locks in its values for later panels. It's also inconsistent with the top level of the same function, which clones each field and calls `cloneDeep` on its config before changing it.

The regression test 'will not write the panel config onto the frames it was given' is deleted along with the fix. It checked that `nested.fields[1].config` and `sourceFrame.fields[1].config` stay `{}`. Without it, nothing catches the in-place change above.
Assertions were removed or rewritten; equivalent replacement coverage has not been established.

findings.message: `resourceVersion` is now deleted only on the update path. On the create path, `obj.metadata` is built by spreading `options.k8s`, so any `resourceVersion` the caller passes (for example '0', or a stale value from an imported or copied dashboard) goes out in the POST to `client.create`. The Kubernetes API server rejects creates where `resourceVersion` is set, so saving a new dashboard in those cases will fail. Before this change it was deleted unconditionally.
The test that checked `resourceVersion` is left out of the create POST was removed instead of updated. That hides the behavior change on the create path, and nothing now covers it.

verdicts.reason: This change undoes a documented performance fix. It puts back the `(\b|\B)` prefix on logsGrammar's 'log-token-key' regex, which causes quadratic backtracking on long log lines with no `=`. It also removes the `foo=bar` key-value test that the note says must keep passing. That is a violation of the logs-grammar note. The other notes are about unrelated test areas, and none of them are outdated.

findings.message: The change puts the `(\b|\B)` prefix back on the 'log-token-key' rule. That prefix matches at every position, so for each start offset the engine runs the greedy `[\w_]+` and then fails the `(?=\s*=)` lookahead. On a long line with no `=` (for example ~16KB), that is quadratic work during Prism tokenization and can freeze the Logs panel main thread. This undoes the earlier fix (~820ms down to ~0.16ms). Keep `/\b[\w_]+(?=\s*=)/gi`.
findings.evidence:
-  'log-token-key': /\b[\w_]+(?=\s*=)/gi,
+  'log-token-key': /(\b|\B)[\w_]+(?=\s*=)/gi,

locations.message: The change deletes the 'Identifies keys in key-value pairs' test. That test checked that `foo=bar` gives a 'log-token-key' token with content `foo`. Without it, nothing in generateLogGrammar's tests checks key-value tokenization, even though this same change edits the key rule.
